    - list:
      - listitem: The ledger is an ordered list labelled with its title, newest first
      - listitem: Undo is labelled with the change and how many changes build on it; Redo with the change
      - listitem: Before → after is plain text; the arrow is read as "to"
    - heading "Motion" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: New changes open their row at the top – the panel grows smoothly – and then fade in
      - listitem: Pointing at Undo lights up the change and everything built on it – "Also undone" in blue, "Can't undo" in amber
      - listitem: Undo draws a line across each row, down the chain a beat after each other; the rows go quiet and their logos gray
      - listitem: Rows never change height – the time, Undo, Redo and the flags all share one slot
      - listitem: With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once
    - heading "Responsive behavior" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: "Built on a container query: under 480px the numbers move to a line of their own, the time drops the system's name and Undo / Redo shrink to round icon buttons"
      - listitem: On touch screens Undo and Redo show on every row, in place of the time
      - listitem: "Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme=\"dark\""
    - heading "Notes for AI" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Give your coding assistant this summary instead of screenshots.
    - list:
      - listitem: Pass every change every time – ids keep rows in place, new ids slide in
      - listitem: at is epoch ms; pass now to drive "2m ago" yourself
      - listitem: Undo calls onUndo with the ids to revert – actually reverting them in Stripe, GitHub etc. is up to you
      - listitem: "Mark irreversible changes with reversible: false – honesty about what can't be undone is the point"
      - listitem: Colors are variables on .ui-ldgc, e.g. --ui-ldgc-also-bg / --ui-ldgc-kept-bg
      - listitem: The undo, redo and lock icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file
